content: Do your human best, then entrust the outcome to heaven.
author: Japanese Proverbs
sourceWork: Jinji wo tsukushite tenmei wo matsu (人事を尽くして天命を待つ)
explanation: True peace of mind does not come from passive fatalism, nor from anxious micromanagement. It is found in the supreme harmony of doing everything within human power with immaculate care, and then completely releasing attachment to the verdict of fate.
practicalInsight: Prepare thoroughly for your presentation or duty, execute with wholehearted focus, and then let go of the applause or outcome.
reflectionPrompt: Are you creating anxiety by trying to control things that belong to fate rather than focusing solely on your effort?
